subproblems.title: Test forms have bounded Euclidean coefficient norm
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be an arbitrary set and let ω ∈ Dⁿ(U) (a TestFormOn U n: a smooth, compactly supported n-form on ℝ^P with tsupport ω ⊆ U). Then there is C ∈ ℝ with C > 0 such that |ω(x)| ≤ C for every x ∈ ℝ^P, where |α| = covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_{I strictly increasing} α(e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(n−1)})²)^{1/2}.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)) (ω : TestFormOn U n), ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ x : Eucl P, covectorEuclideanNorm ((ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) n) x) ≤ C
subproblems.natural_proof:
ROLE IN THE SELECTED PROOF. This is Step 2 of the supplied proof: for a test form ω, g(x) := covectorEuclideanNorm(ω(x)) is continuous with compact support, hence bounded. The parent uses the positive bound C supplied here in place of c = B + 1.

REUSE. This is the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.br_la_testForm_covectorNorm_bounded of DAG node root.boundary_rectifiability-a1.lattice_approximation-a1.testform_bounded-a1 (status accepted, candidate commit c34586955a827a6731d9bc0ca8ae1ba1c0791948, equal to its published workspace result commit). Its title, statement and frozen Lean type are copied byte-for-byte from dag.json, so no new node is created. The numbered proof below is that node's accepted argument, which coincides with Step 2 of the supplied proof. It proves exactly the statement above from its hypotheses.

Notation. An n-covector α on ℝ^P is a continuous alternating map (ℝ^P)ⁿ → ℝ, and |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α = √(Σ_{I : Fin n → Fin P} [I strictly increasing] α(e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(n−1)})²). Here e_i = EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ i, and the bracket means the summand is 0 when I is not strictly increasing. ω ∈ TestFormOn U n means that ω : ℝ^P → Λⁿ is C^∞ (ContDiff ℝ ∞), has compact support, and satisfies tsupport ω ⊆ U.

Proof.
1. (α ↦ |α| is continuous.) Fix I : Fin n → Fin P and put v_I := (e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(n−1)}). Evaluation α ↦ α(v_I) is continuous on the space of continuous alternating maps (ContinuousAlternatingMap.instContinuousEvalConst; Continuous.eval_const). So the summand α ↦ [I strictly increasing] α(v_I)² is continuous: it is the square of a continuous function when I is strictly increasing, and the constant 0 otherwise. The sum over the finite type Fin n → Fin P is continuous (continuous_finsetSum), and so is its composition with the continuous square root (Real.continuous_sqrt).
2. (f is continuous.) ω is C^∞ (the first component of the test-form property), hence continuous. So f(x) := |ω(x)| is continuous, as the composition of x ↦ ω(x) with the map of Step 1. Concretely, each x ↦ ω(x)(v_I) is continuous, and f is the square root of a finite sum of their squares and zeros.
3. (f has compact support.) If ω(x) = 0, then f(x) = |0| = 0, because every summand is 0² or 0 and √0 = 0 (covectorEuclideanNorm_zero). So support f ⊆ support ω ⊆ tsupport ω. Since ω has compact support, so does f (HasCompactSupport.mono').
4. (Boundedness.) A continuous, compactly supported real-valued function on ℝ^P is bounded (Continuous.bounded_above_of_compact_support). So there is C₀ ∈ ℝ with |f(x)| ≤ C₀ for all x ∈ ℝ^P. In particular C₀ ≥ |f(0)| ≥ 0.
5. (Conclusion.) Put C := C₀ + 1. Then C ≥ 1 > 0, and for every x ∈ ℝ^P we have f(x) ≤ |f(x)| ≤ C₀ < C, that is, covectorEuclideanNorm(ω(x)) ≤ C. ∎
proof_key_steps: α ↦ |α| is continuous: evaluations of continuous alternating maps at fixed tuples are continuous, then a finite sum of squares (or zeros) and a square root.
x ↦ |ω(x)| is continuous because ω is smooth, and has compact support because ω does and |0| = 0.
A continuous compactly supported real function is bounded by some C₀ ≥ 0; take C := C₀ + 1 > 0.

subproblems.title: Mass estimate |T(ω)| ≤ M_W(T)·sup|ω| for test forms supported in W
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U W : Set (Eucl P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (ω : TestFormOn U n) (B C : ℝ), 0 ≤ B → T.massOn W ≤ ENNReal.ofReal B → tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) n) ⊆ W → (∀ x, covectorEuclideanNorm ((ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) n) x) ≤ C) → |T ω| ≤ B * C
subproblems.natural_proof:
ROLE IN THE SELECTED PROOF. This is Steps 3–4 of the supplied proof: homogeneity of the coefficient norm, admissibility of the rescalings ±ω/c, and le_massOn. It is stated with an explicit real bound B for M_W(T) and an explicit pointwise bound C for |ω|. The parent applies it with W := U and B := 0, which it may do because T.massOn U = T.mass = 0 = ENNReal.ofReal 0.

REUSE. This is the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.cmb_abs_apply_le_of_massOn_le of DAG node root.compactness_mass_bounds-a1.mass_bound-a1 (status accepted, candidate commit ba202ac0407b6e93210594416fcd0729874b2eff, equal to its published workspace result commit). Its title, statement and frozen Lean type are copied byte-for-byte from dag.json, so no new node is created. The numbered proof below is that node's accepted argument, and it proves exactly the statement above from its hypotheses. It never divides by C, so the case C = 0 needs no separate treatment.

Notation. |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α = √(Σ_{I : Fin n → Fin P} [I strictly increasing] α(e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(n−1)})²), with e_i = EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ i and summand 0 when I is not strictly increasing. M_W(T) = T.massOn W = sup{ENNReal.ofReal(T(ψ)) : ψ ∈ massAdmissibleOn U n W}, where massAdmissibleOn U n W = {ψ ∈ TestFormOn U n : tsupport ψ ⊆ W and |ψ(x)| ≤ 1 for all x}.

Proof.
1. (Homogeneity.) For t ∈ ℝ and an n-covector α, |tα| = |t|·|α|. Indeed (tα)(v) = t·α(v) for every tuple v. So each strictly increasing summand α(v_I)² becomes t²·α(v_I)², and every other summand stays 0. The sum S therefore becomes t²·S (Finset.mul_sum), and √(t²·S) = √(t²)·√S = |t|·√S (Real.sqrt_mul with t² ≥ 0; Real.sqrt_sq_eq_abs).
2. (C ≥ 0.) 0 ≤ |ω(0)| ≤ C, by covectorEuclideanNorm_nonneg and the pointwise hypothesis at x = 0.
3. (Admissible rescalings.) Fix a real c > C; then c > 0 by Step 2. Let s ∈ {c⁻¹, −c⁻¹}, so |s| = c⁻¹. Since TestFormOn U n is a real submodule, s•ω ∈ TestFormOn U n. Its support satisfies tsupport(s•ω) ⊆ tsupport ω ⊆ W (tsupport_smul_subset_right and the support hypothesis). By Step 1, for every x, |(s•ω)(x)| = |s·ω(x)| = c⁻¹·|ω(x)|, and c⁻¹·|ω(x)| ≤ 1 because |ω(x)| ≤ C < c. Hence s•ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn U n W, and GeometricCurrentOn.le_massOn gives ENNReal.ofReal(T(s•ω)) ≤ M_W(T) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal B.
4. (Unpacking.) Because B ≥ 0, ENNReal.ofReal a ≤ ENNReal.ofReal B implies a ≤ B (ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal_iff). By linearity of T, T(s•ω) = s·T(ω). So c⁻¹·T(ω) ≤ B and −c⁻¹·T(ω) ≤ B. Multiplying by c > 0 gives T(ω) ≤ B·c and −T(ω) ≤ B·c, that is, |T(ω)| ≤ B·c. This holds for every real c > C.
5. (Letting c decrease to C.) Let ε > 0 and put c := C + ε/(B + 1). Since B + 1 > 0, c > C. Step 4 gives |T(ω)| ≤ B·C + B·ε/(B + 1) ≤ B·C + ε, because 0 ≤ B ≤ B + 1 and ε/(B + 1) > 0. Since ε > 0 was arbitrary, |T(ω)| ≤ B·C (le_of_forall_pos_le_add). ∎
proof_key_steps: Homogeneity |tα| = |t|·|α| of the coefficient norm, and C ≥ 0 from the pointwise bound at x = 0.
For every c > C, both ±c⁻¹ω are mass-admissible for W, so le_massOn, the mass hypothesis, B ≥ 0 and linearity give ±c⁻¹T(ω) ≤ B, hence |T(ω)| ≤ B·c.
Let c decrease to C (c = C + ε/(B + 1), ε > 0 arbitrary) to obtain |T(ω)| ≤ B·C.
